$comment: Source fields a review resolved by reading a publisher's data, applied by `buildSourceRegister` over the rows it derives from the research CSV. An input to the build rather than an edit of its output, for the same reason as `license-decisions.json`: the build rewrites the register whole, so a field recorded in the output is erased by the next run with no error and a normal-looking count.
$whyNotTheCSV: The research CSV records `address_role`, `coverage` and `upstream` as the placeholders `varies`, `country-specific` and the empty string on all 389 of its non-rail rows, and has no column for a personal-data review. That CSV is the record of what one research pass found on 2026-09-18, so a later review records its own findings here rather than by rewriting the pass's record.
$shape:
Each key is a `sourceID` the register declares. Each value carries any of `addressRoles`, `coverage`, `upstreamLineage`, `personalDataReview` and `adapterID`, which replace the derived row's values. See `@mailwoman/corpus/source-register`'s `AddressSourceRecord`.

`adapterID` names the corpus adapter that emits this source's rows, and a release-eligible build admits a row only through it. `readSourceEligibility` keys each source by `<adapterID>:<ISO2>` and `createIneligibilityReader` looks a row up by its own `source` and `country`, because the register scopes a source to one publisher in one jurisdiction while one adapter can serve several: `ban` emits eleven jurisdictions from one schema. A source that declares no adapter stays out of that map, which is correct rather than restrictive, since no adapter emits it and no row can arrive under it.
$addressRoles: Keyed by the address column's path in the published record, because a publication can carry two roles on one record. `ingestEligibilityProblems` requires at least one column to have a role.
$upstreamLineage: The endpoint or dataset this source's copy was taken from, so two register rows fed by one upstream submission count as one observation rather than two. A URL when the upstream is not itself a register row.
$banRepetition: Ten rows below are one database, IGN's Base Adresse Nationale, split by the INSEE department code each file is published under. `coverage` differs per territory because each is a measurement of that territory's file, and `addressRoles`, `upstreamLineage` and `personalDataReview` repeat because the column layout and the publisher's non-nominative characterisation are the BAN's and identical throughout. France's own row, `fr-property-building-1`, is the eleventh file of the same database and carries its own measurement of the whole-country extract. The license decisions point at the shared reading `ign-ban-lov2-territories`.
$sireneRepetition: Nine rows below are one source, INSEE's SIRENE establishment register, split by overseas territory. The fields repeat because the register carries one row per jurisdiction and each row's coverage statement is about that territory, while the column layout and the diffusion mechanism are SIRENE's and identical throughout.
$sireneSecondAddress: SIRENE's establishment file carries a second address family, the `2`-suffixed columns, which INSEE labels only `adresse secondaire` — `complementAdresse2Etablissement` reads `Complément d'adresse secondaire`. What role that address plays is unstated, so it takes no entry in `addressRoles` rather than a guessed one, and the coverage text names it so a reader knows the column exists.
$ocdsPartyRoles: An OCDS release keys its addresses by party role, so `addressRoles` names roles rather than columns for those sources. A role is assigned only where OCDS's own codelist defines it, retrieved from `https://standard.open-contracting.org/1.1/en/codelists/partyRole.csv`: `buyer`, `procuringEntity`, `payer`, `funder` and `reviewBody` are bodies acting in the process, so their address is an office they operate and reads `facility`; `supplier` and `tenderer` are the transacting party, so theirs reads `counterparty`. Germany's release also uses eight roles from an extension whose codelist neither the 1.1 nor the latest list defines — `processContactPoint`, `reviewContactPoint`, `submissionReceiptBody`, `mediationBody`, `evaluationBody`, `procurementServiceProvider`, `leadTenderer`, `subcontractor` — and those take no role here rather than a guessed one.

es-mixed-regulatory-1.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of the Dirección General del Catastro, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://www.catastro.hacienda.gob.es/INSPIRE/Addresses/ES.SDGC.AD.atom.xml`, 681,783 bytes, sha256 `4342d37b6d5527eb7b8bebadc97966c90f1a041068ae9398b90183f2176898b9`, carrying `<updated>2026-08-21T00:00:00Z</updated>`. The feed lists 55 entries, and this row covers 52 of them. The other three belong to the Provincial Councils of Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa and Navarra, which publish their own cadastres through the same feed and state their own terms, `CC BY 3.0 ES`, `CC-BY-SA` and `CC BY 4.0`. Adding them needs a row each, because a decision scoped to one publisher cannot reach another. Each of the 52 entries links a province feed listing one zipped GML per municipality. The measured instance is Ceuta, `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.zip`, 354,647 bytes, whose one member `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` is 11,861,975 bytes and holds 8,126 `AD:Address` features. A feature is a point at a building entrance carrying a house-number designator, and it references a thoroughfare name, a postal descriptor and an administrative unit by `xlink:href`. The row count for the other 51 offices was not measured.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` was counted over all 11,861,975 bytes, so this covers the file rather than its first features. It holds 48 distinct element names and none of them names a party: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element, and no personal name of any kind. The only names are 505 `AD:ThoroughfareName`, 5 `AD:PostalDescriptor` and 1 `AD:AdminUnitName`. The file declares the INSPIRE Addresses 3.0 schema at `urn:x-inspire:specification:gmlas:Addresses:3.0`, which has no party element for another municipality to populate, so the reading rests on the schema as well as on the one municipality read. This is what separates the row from the other 25 `verified-corpus` sources: each of those is a business register or a procurement portal where the address belongs to a party, and some of those parties are natural persons trading on their own account. The cadastre's AD theme records the place. The ownership data that Spanish cadastral records also hold travels through a separate protected channel and appears nowhere in this dataset.

dk-property-building-1.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of Klimadatastyrelsen, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://www2.sdfe.dk/INSPIRE/feeds/Addresses.xml`, 3,130 bytes, sha256 `5a32be44b186586dbef5efa24bd200b3d2d85afebb74172250f5dd977d3ddbea`. Denmark serves this theme as a GeoPackage rather than as GML, which is why `addressRoles` is keyed by a table name instead of an element name. The feed holds one entry covering the whole country. Its dataset is `DK_INSPIRE_Addresses.zip`, 101,406,038 bytes, sha256 `0b4e13e27307659ac64065e8f67301b4eb649faa35e6e29f8f443f51c91c5141`, whose member `ad_inspire.gpkg` is 391,258,112 bytes. The database declares five tables in `gpkg_contents`: `address` with 599,999 rows, `thoroughfarename` with 112,488, `addressareaname` with 7,840, `postaldescriptor` with 1,089 and `adminunitname` with 105. **Treat 599,999 as a possible export cap rather than as Denmark's address count**: it is one short of a round 600,000, and the national address register holds several times that. Establishing the true extent means asking the publisher or finding a second distribution. Two reader notes. The feed writes its one entry as `<entry xml:lang="da">`, so a reader matching a bare `<entry>` finds none. And the Atom entry's href returns the weblink's listing page; the file needs `&realfilename=DK_INSPIRE_Addresses.zip` appended.

personalDataReview.because: Every column of every table the GeoPackage declares was listed, so this covers the database's whole schema rather than a sample of its rows. The five tables carry 39, 16, 15, 15 and 15 columns, and none of the 100 identifies a party: there is no owner, holder, occupant or contact column, and no personal name. Every column of the `address` table is INSPIRE address structure, being an identifier, a lifespan date, a position, a locator designator, or a reference to a thoroughfare name, postal descriptor, administrative unit, parcel or building. One value invites a misreading: `position_method` reads `byotherparty`, which is an INSPIRE codelist term for how the position was determined rather than a reference to a party. The schema is the INSPIRE Addresses model, which has no party element.

pl-property-building-1.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of Główny Urząd Geodezji i Kartografii, reached as a WFS 2.0 download service at `https://mapy.geoportal.gov.pl/wss/service/INSPIRE/Addresses`. **Measured 8,625,921 `ms:AD.Address` features on 2026-10-01, and the service states none of that itself.** It answers a bare `resultType=hits` with `numberMatched="1000"`, which is MapServer's default feature cap, the same request at `startIndex=1` with `1`, and a feature page with `numberMatched="unknown"`. The count comes from `countWFSFeaturesByPaging` in `@mailwoman/core/api`, which takes the largest `startIndex` that still returns a feature by doubling and then bisecting: 51 requests, with a page of 5 at index 8,625,919 returning exactly the 2 the count implies. **The payload is the Polish register's own schema rather than the harmonised INSPIRE Addresses model.** A feature is a MapServer row whose element names are the register's columns, so a build needs no join across feature types and no component resolution: `adres` carries the whole address as one string, as in `Piotrków Trybunalski 1 Maja 10`, beside `miejscowosc`, `ulica`, `numer` and `kod` separately, with `teryt`, `simc` and `ulic` as the national register codes. The service publishes this one feature type, and no `ad:ThoroughfareName`, `ad:PostalDescriptor` or `ad:AdminUnitName` type exists to join to. The theme derives from the Państwowy Rejestr Granic, and the feature ids name their upstream register, as in `PL.ZIPIN.3742.EMUiA_9945001100000172050`, which is the municipal address register EMUiA. It serves four GML flavours and no JSON, so a build reads GML. One caution: the service's `inspire_dls:SpatialDataSetIdentifier` states the literal `mycode`, an unreplaced placeholder, so the per-feature-type `MetadataURL` is what ties this service to its dataset record.

personalDataReview.because: This service publishes the Polish register's schema rather than the INSPIRE model, so the review asks what its columns are rather than whether `AD:LocatorName` is populated. Over 1,000 features read across 40 windows spread through the 8,625,921, reaching 116 distinct localities, the features carry 19 element names and never a twentieth. All 19 are address or register structure: `id`, `gml_id` and `lokalnyid` are identifiers, `jednostkaadmnistracyjna` is the administrative-unit path, `miejscowosc`, `miejscowosc_lower` and `czescmiejscowosci` are locality spellings, `ulica`, `ulica_pol` and `ulica_skr` are street spellings, `numer` is the house number, `kod` is the postcode, `teryt`, `simc` and `ulic` are national register codes, `status` and the dates `data_od` and `wazny_od` are lifecycle fields, and `adres` is the concatenation of the others. None of the 19 names an owner, occupant, holder or contact, and the register this derives from records addressable units rather than their residents. Two columns are present on every feature and populated on none of the 1,000: `status` and `czescmiejscowosci`. The street columns are populated on 741 of 1,000, which is the share of sampled addresses sitting on a named street rather than on a locality alone. A name-shape test flags 119 `ulica` values and 113 `miejscowosc` values as carrying two capitalised words, and reading them settles what that is: Polish streets are commonly named for people, as in `kard. Stefana Wyszyńskiego`, `Krzysztofa Kamila Baczyńskiego` and `księdza Biskupa Władysława Bandurskiego`, and multi-word place names account for the rest, as in `Piotrków Trybunalski` and `Nakło nad Notecią`. A commemorative street name is the name of a street, and both columns are place elements by definition, so neither identifies a party to the address.

The service publishes all five AD feature types and advertises `ImplementsResultPaging`, so a build pages each type rather than downloading a file. Measured 2026-10-01, `resultType=hits` past index 0 reports 1,704,196 `ad:Address` features, 29,315 `ad:ThoroughfareName`, 3,015 `ad:AdminUnitName`, 1,769 `ad:AddressAreaName` and 1,415 `ad:PostalDescriptor`, and a page of each type agreed with its count. personalDataReview.because: Every property of all five feature types was listed, over 40 features each: 10 on `ad:Address`, 10 on `ad:AdminUnitName`, 8 on `ad:AddressAreaName`, 8 on `ad:PostalDescriptor` and 8 on `ad:ThoroughfareName`. None of the 44 identifies a party, and each is INSPIRE address structure, being an identifier, a lifespan or validity date, a status, a position, a locator, a name, a postcode or a component reference. `AD:LocatorName` is the element that needs its own statement, because it is free text of type `GeographicalName` and the one way a family name or a business name reaches an INSPIRE address. This service omits it structurally: its `locator` object carries `designator` and `level` and no `name` key at all, and the designator values are address numbers typed `LocatorDesignatorTypeValue/addressNumber`. The sampled measurement agrees, at 0 of 800 addresses over 40 windows spread across the 1,704,196. The traversal was checked against Estonia, which populates the element on every address, to establish that a reader finding nothing here is reading a service that writes nothing rather than failing to look: Estonia flattens the path to `locator_addresslocator_name_locatorname_name_spelling_text` while Slovakia nests it, so each service needs its own traversal and a single reader run against both would have reported one of them wrongly.

ch-property-building-1.coverage: The official directory of building addresses, published by swisstopo from the Federal Statistical Office's Buildings and Dwellings Register supplemented with cadastral survey data. `amtliches-gebaeudeadressverzeichnis_ch_2056.csv.zip` is 143,235,177 bytes and its single member is 468,306,734 bytes. **Measured 3,303,210 data rows on 2026-10-01**, 17 columns, every row holding exactly 17 fields. The address is assembled from `STN_LABEL`, `ADR_NUMBER`, `ZIP_LABEL`, `COM_NAME` and `COM_CANTON`, with street labels in German, French and Italian as the canton dictates, so one file carries `Grellingerstrasse`, `Route du Clos` and `Via Cantonale`. `ADR_STATUS` reads `real` on 3,251,832 rows and `planned` on 51,378, so 1.56% of the file describes an address that does not yet exist. `BDG_CATEGORY` splits the file usefully: `residential` 1,605,916, `non_residential` 1,258,886, `other_residential` 221,041, `special` 129,630, `partly_residential` 84,901 and `temporary` 2,836. **The publisher states a coverage caveat**: in fewer than ten municipalities the directory is not yet available or not fully available, pending harmonisation of the cadastral survey and register data. personalDataReview.because: **This is the first address publication in the register whose free-text name column carries natural persons' names, and it is why that column is opened rather than assumed empty.** Sixteen of the 17 columns are structure: identifiers (`ADR_EGAID`, `STR_ESID`, `BDG_EGID`, `ADR_EDID`), a street label, a house number, a building category, a postcode and place, a municipality number, name and canton, a status, an official flag, a modification date and a position. The seventeenth is `BDG_NAME`, a free-text building name, populated on 20,989 of the 3,303,210 rows, which is 0.64%. Every populated value was read rather than sampled: 1,158 match a two-capitalised-word shape, of which 684 carry a structure word in German, French or Italian and describe a building, as `Garage Romiglios`, `Einstellgarage Beltrametti`, `Alphütte Pürt` and `Résidence La Pran` do. The remaining 474 were read individually, and most are Italian-language building and facility names concentrated in Ticino, as `Monti Incella`, `Capanna Basodino`, `Officine SBB CFF FFS` and `Azienda Agricola` are. **At least twelve are a surname and a given name on a row whose `BDG_CATEGORY` reads `residential`**: `Chaignat Aimée` in Jura, `Rutz Nelly`, `Maggiorini Tullio`, `Maggiorini Jole`, `Frigerio Cesare Vittorio`, `Stern Flavia`, `Pozzi Castelli Tamara`, `MTI DELLA COSTA-GUIDOTTI RENZO`, `TRAVERSE-MEILI PFEIFFER`, `TRAVERSE-LANDOLT ARMIN` and `RONCO BALINO-KUHN` in Ticino, and `NB EFH Lauber Jörg` in Valais. A surname and a given name beside a residential address identifies a natural person at their home, which is the class `ingestEligibilityProblems` refuses and which this repository decided on 2026-09-30 it would not carry. A further set pairs a surname with a structure word, as `Autounterstand Scherrer`, `Holzbaracke Tscherrig`, `Carport Stuck` and `Dépôt Fournier Georges` do, and whether those name an owner or a business is not settled here. **Whether a build that never reads `BDG_NAME` changes this reading is a question for the operator and counsel rather than for this record**: the 16 remaining columns carry no party, and the register records the source as published.

personalDataReview.because: SIRENE registers `entrepreneurs individuels`, so a row can name a natural person and give an address for them. INSEE records an objection per row and places the obligation on the reuser: `il est ainsi de votre responsabilité de tenir compte du statut de diffusion le plus récent de chaque personne physique`. A row whose `statutDiffusionEtablissement` reads `P` is diffused partially after an objection, and for a natural person `l'identité de l'entrepreneur (nom, prénoms…), l'adresse dans la commune et la géolocalisation seront masquées`. That status changes after a corpus is built, so a frozen corpus and a model trained on it keep an address INSEE has since stopped diffusing. Filtering on the status is mechanical; discharging a continuing obligation from a published artifact is the open question.

personalDataReview.because: The publication names natural persons and carries addresses for them. Measured on the 2022 release: 149 of 17,373 distinct supplier names take the `Surname, Firstname` form over 179 rows, 43 of those rows carrying a street line, and `Upton, David Gregory` is published at `3 Sloan Rd, Hawthorndene SA 5051`. A sole trader's reported address can be their home, and the record does not distinguish the two. The analysis that would move this to `assessed` is a decision rather than a measurement, and the measurement it would rest on is in the retained receipt.
